claims.text: The starting FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloy has an FCC structure.
The starting alloy has soft-ferromagnetic properties similar to previously studied FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt alloys.
Severe plastic deformation followed by controlled low-temperature annealing will produce a nanocrystalline microstructure while limiting grain growth.
Controlled low-temperature annealing after severe plastic deformation will relieve internal stresses.
The proposed processing will produce a high density of grain boundaries and retained dislocation defects.
Grain boundaries and deformation defects introduced by severe plastic deformation act as pinning centers for magnetic domain walls.
The processed microstructure creates a higher local magnetic-anisotropy distribution.
Greater domain-wall pinning will increase the coercive field.
The processed alloy will have higher coercivity than conventionally cast and slowly cooled FeCoNi-based soft-ferromagnetic alloys.
The coercivity increase can occur without a substantial loss of saturation magnetization.
Conventionally processed equiatomic FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt alloys exhibit soft ferromagnetism.
The coercivity benefit requires retention of a nanocrystalline microstructure.
Excessive annealing will cause grain growth that negates the proposed coercivity increase.
Formation of secondary phases would likely negate the proposed coercivity increase.
